canonical_statement: The study aimed to develop a domain-specific retrieval-augmented generation system for reliable, context-specific biomedical citation recommendation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This study aims to develop a domain-specific RAG system for reliable, context-specific biomedical citation recommendations.

canonical_statement: The sentence-level citation recommendation task was defined as ranking articles that provide relevant context or evidence for a supplied biomedical query sentence.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Given a clinical query or sentence Q, the goal is to generate a ranked list of articles A such that each Ai provides relevant context or evidence for Q.

canonical_statement: CiteSure used a two-stage pipeline in which BioLLM2Vec maximized candidate recall, BioRankLLaMA reranked candidates for precision, and an LLM generated citation recommendations from the top-ranked evidence.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: First, the dense retriever BioLLM2Vec retrieves a broad set of candidate articles ... maximizing recall. Next, the reranker BioRankLLaMA assigns relevance scores ... optimizing precision. These top references are then used as augmented input for the LLM.

canonical_statement: Figure 1 depicted data construction from PubMed Central articles and introduction-sentence citations, followed by BioLLM2Vec pre-ranking, BioRankLLaMA reranking, and LLM-based augmented generation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Figure 1. The overview structure of our study.

canonical_statement: The Alzheimer’s disease source corpus contained 12,869 primary articles from the PubMed Central Open Access Subset available as of September 23, 2023.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We collected all available articles on Alzheimer’s disease from the PubMed Central Open Access Subset as of September 23, 2023, resulting in a corpus of 12869 primary articles.

population.label: Alzheimer’s disease primary articles in the PubMed Central Open Access Subset as of 2023-09-23

canonical_statement: Expanding the corpus with articles cited by the primary articles produced a candidate collection of 255,749 reference articles.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We then expanded this set by including all articles cited within these primary articles, yielding a candidate collection of 255749 reference articles.

population.label: Candidate cited-reference articles

canonical_statement: Candidate articles were represented by title and abstract rather than full text to support scalable retrieval.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Each article’s abstract and title were preserved, enabling focused retrieval based on high-level content without processing full texts, thus balancing relevance with efficiency.

canonical_statement: The authors reported verifying that each citing–cited article pair represented a true citation relationship.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We have verified that each citing–cited article pair in our dataset corresponds to a true citation relationship.

canonical_statement: Segmenting introduction sections and retaining sentences with at least one citation yielded 560,372 sentence–citation samples.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: By selecting sentences that contain at least 1 reference, we constructed positive citation pairs ... This process yielded 560372 sentences and their citations.

population.label: Introduction sentences containing at least one cited reference

canonical_statement: Each sentence-level training record included the sentence text, the PMIDs cited within that sentence, and the PMID of the source article.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Specifically, we extracted (1) the sentence text, (2) references cited within the sentence (identified by PubMed IDs), and (3) the origin article’s PubMed ID (PMID).

canonical_statement: BioLLM2Vec was fine-tuned from LLaMA3-8B-Instruct using 20,966 sentence-level examples selected from sentences containing four to five citations.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: BioLLM2Vec is fine-tuned on the LLaMA3-8B-Instruct model ... We curated a subset of 20 966 sentences ... selecting sentences with 4-5 citations.

canonical_statement: For BioLLM2Vec training, articles cited by the query sentence were positives and 15 articles cited elsewhere in the same paper but not by the sentence or its context were negatives.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Articles directly cited by the sentence were designated as positive samples ... First, 15 negatives were chosen by identifying articles cited within the same paper but not by the specific sentence or its context.

canonical_statement: BioLLM2Vec training also used 185 hard negatives per query selected from top LLM-Embedder results that were not cited by the sentence.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Second, we included ranked hard negatives, selecting 185 top-ranked articles by an initial LLM-based retriever (LLM-Embedder) that were not cited in the sentence.

canonical_statement: BioLLM2Vec was optimized with contrastive loss to increase cosine similarity between query sentences and cited articles while decreasing similarity to negative articles.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We trained BioLLM2Vec with contrastive loss to maximize the similarity between query sentences and their positive samples while minimizing similarity to negative samples.

canonical_statement: BioLLM2Vec training used eight A100 GPUs, LoRA-based memory optimization, a learning rate of 2e-5, batch size 64, and FlashAttention.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The training utilized 8 A100 GPUs with LoRA-based memory optimization, a learning rate of 2e-5, a batch size of 64, and FlashAttention.

canonical_statement: BioRankLLaMA was trained on 22,704 sentence-level examples, each associated with four to five citations.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: BioRankLLaMA was also trained using 22 704 sentences ... each associated with 4-5 citations.

canonical_statement: For each BioRankLLaMA query, cited articles were positives and 15 highly ranked but uncited BioLLM2Vec results were negatives.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We still take citations of the query sentence as positive samples. ... we generated 15 negative examples per query sentence from top highly relevant but not cited articles ranked by BioLLM2Vec.

canonical_statement: BioRankLLaMA fine-tuning used eight A100 GPUs, LoRA-based memory optimization, learning rate 2e-5, batch size 64, bfloat16 precision, and FlashAttention.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Fine-tuning was conducted on 8 A100 GPUs, using LoRA-based memory optimization, a learning rate of 2e-5, a batch size of 64, bfloat16 precision, and FlashAttention.

canonical_statement: At inference, BioLLM2Vec retrieved a top-N candidate set (example N=200), BioRankLLaMA reranked it to a top-K set (example K=10), and the LLM selected and explained five citations.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Using BioLLM2Vec ... select the top-N (eg, N = 200) ... apply BioRankLLaMA ... identifying the top-K (eg, K = 10) ... prompt the LLM to re-rank these 10 papers ... and recommend the 5 most relevant papers.

canonical_statement: The generation prompt requested title, authors, publication year, venue, PMID, and a relevance rationale for each recommended paper.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: For each recommended paper, provide the following metadata: title, authors, publication year, venue, PMID, and rationale.

canonical_statement: The main evaluation set contained 505 Alzheimer’s disease sentences, each paired with five gold-standard references.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We used a test set of 505 sentences from the Alzheimer’s disease dataset, with each sentence paired with 5 gold-standard references.

population.label: Alzheimer’s disease test sentences with five gold-standard references each

canonical_statement: Overall citation evaluation compared standalone GPT-4o, GPT-4, GPT-3.5, and LLaMA3.1-70B-Instruct with BM25, MedCPT, repLLaMA–rankLLaMA, BioLLM2Vec–BioRankLLaMA, a general-domain RAG baseline, and CiteSure variants.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The pure LLMs include ... GPT-4o, GPT-4, GPT-3.5, and ... LLaMA3.1-70B-Instruct. The second category includes ... BM25 and MedCPT ... repLLaMA–rankLLaMA and BioLLM2Vec-BioRankLLaMA.

canonical_statement: Factual accuracy was defined as the proportion of recommended citations whose complete metadata could be verified in PubMed.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Each citation was verified against PubMed, with a citation considered factually accurate if all its metadata could be confirmed in the PubMed database. The factual accuracy is calculated as the proportion of correct references across the test set.

outcome.definition: Proportion of citations with all metadata verified in PubMed
outcome.measurement_method: PubMed metadata verification

canonical_statement: The automated relevance evaluator compared each citation’s title and abstract with the query sentence using GPT-4o, scoring relevant citations as 1 and non-relevant citations as 0; the Methods state that fabricated citations also received 0.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Fabricated citations automatically received a relevance score of 0. For non-fabricated citations, relevance was evaluated by comparing the citation’s title and abstract with the query sentence, using GPT-4o as an automated evaluator. Citations marked as relevant were scored as 1, while non-relevant ones received a score of 0.

outcome.definition: Binary relevance of a candidate citation to a query sentence
outcome.measurement_method: GPT-4o yes/no evaluator using title and abstract

canonical_statement: Broad retrieval evaluation measured the proportion of 505 query sentences for which at least one of five gold references appeared among the top 100 results retrieved from 255,749 candidates.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: For each query, we let models retrieve the top 100 most relevant articles from a pool of 255 749 candidates. We calculated the proportion of sentences for which at least 1 gold-standard reference appeared among the top 100 retrieved articles.

canonical_statement: Reranking evaluation used 20 candidates per query—five gold references and 15 BioLLM2Vec-ranked negatives—and reported Recall, MAP, MRR, and Precision@5.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: BioRankLLaMA was tested with a candidate set of 20 references per query sentence, consisting of the 5 gold-standard references and 15 additional negative samples ... We calculate ... Recall, Mean Average Precision (MAP), Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR), and Precision@5.

canonical_statement: The human factuality evaluation randomly sampled 30 test sentences and assessed five citations per sentence from each of GPT-4o and LLaMA3.1-70B-Instruct.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We first conducted a human evaluation on a randomly sampled subset of 30 test sentences. For each sentence ... 5 citations ... generated by ... GPT-4o and ... LLaMA 3.1-70B-Instruct.

population.label: Randomly sampled test sentences in the human factuality evaluation

canonical_statement: Two annotators independently checked citation title, authors, and publication details against Medline and Google Scholar and reached full consensus; the authors did not calculate inter-annotator agreement because the task was factual verification.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: They verified each generated citation by cross-referencing Medline and Google Scholar ... inter-annotator agreement metrics were not applicable. Both annotators reached full consensus through independent verification.

canonical_statement: The authors concluded that CiteSure’s two-stage domain-specific RAG framework improved citation reliability and contextual relevance over standalone LLM and general retrieval baselines.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: By combining a biomedical-trained retriever (BioLLM2Vec) and reranker (BioRankLLaMA), CiteSure effectively mitigates citation hallucination and enhances contextual relevance.

canonical_statement: The authors concluded that domain-specific adaptation was valuable for improving biomedical citation reliability and semantic precision.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: These findings underscore the value of domain-specific adaptation in improving citation reliability and semantic precision.

canonical_statement: The authors stated that CiteSure’s modular retriever–reranker design could be extended to broader biomedical corpora and large-scale repositories.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: CiteSure’s design is inherently generalizable to broader biomedical corpora. The modular retriever–reranker architecture allows direct deployment across PubMed or other large-scale repositories.

canonical_statement: The authors positioned CiteSure as a citation-transparency and verification tool rather than a system for generating or justifying unsupported claims.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: CiteSure is intended as a tool for improving the transparency and accuracy of citation practices rather than for generating or justifying unsupported claims.

canonical_statement: Training and evaluation were limited to an Alzheimer’s disease dataset, which may limit generalizability to other biomedical domains.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We trained and evaluated our methods exclusively on the Alzheimer’s disease dataset, which may limit generalizability to other biomedical domains.

canonical_statement: The retriever and reranker were built on LLaMA3-8B-Instruct rather than newer base models.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We used LLaMA3-8b-instruct as the backbone for training the domain-specific retriever and reranker. As newer base models ... continue to advance ... future iterations ... will incorporate these updated backbones.

canonical_statement: Automated relevance scoring may be biased because GPT-4o was both the CiteSure generative backbone and the relevance evaluator.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Since relevance scoring in our evaluation relied on GPT-4o as an automatic evaluator, potential bias may arise because GPT-4o also serves as the generative backbone within CiteSure.

canonical_statement: Learning from real-world citation patterns may conflate contextual relevance with citation frequency and favor highly cited or high-impact journals.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Because CiteSure is trained on real-world citation patterns, it may conflate contextual relevance with citation frequency, potentially favoring highly cited or high-impact journals.

canonical_statement: Using only titles and abstracts may omit supporting evidence that appears in full text.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Although abstracts may omit supporting evidence residing in the full text ... Future work will expand this framework to section-level and full-text retrieval.
